newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BEATEN PSG MUST TURN QUICKLY BACK TO LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BEATEN PSG MUST TURN QUICKLY BACK TO LEAGUE.

text.p: Paris St Germain, having relinquished the European Cup Winners' Cup, barely have enough time to turn their attention back to the French first division and a crucial trip to arch-rivals Marseille on Saturday.

"It's going to be very, very difficult, it's true. But then, we're playing for second place, it's important," coach Ricardo said as he faced the tough task of reorientating his players after their 1-0 defeat by Barcelona in Rotterdam on Wednesday.
PSG are three points ahead of third-placed Nantes with two games left in a championship already won by Monaco.
The Parisians, who close the season at home to Strasbourg on May 24, are hoping to clinch France's second berth in the European Cup next season.
Otherwise, they would go into a UEFA Cup which will no longer include domestic runners-up from the larger European leagues.
Ricardo said his team had contributed in equal measure to Barcelona to a very good final and confirmed their European pedigree.
"We're not just anybody. We have to continue on this path. By persevering like this people will talk about PSG as they do about Barca.
"I have nothing to reproach my players for, they were very good," the Brazilian former PSG central defender said.

Bruno N'Gotty, who French commentators said only put one foot wrong all night when he gave away the penalty from which Brazil's Ronaldo scored Barcelona's goal, was confident PSG would not suffer after-effects at Marseille.

"This result is not worrying in relation to Marseille," said the central defender who scored when PSG beat Rapid Vienna to lift the Cup Winners' Cup last year. "It's our second challenge of the week and we'll win that one.
"If we play as we did this (Wednesday) evening, that will be good. We've had our slumps (this season). But against Barca, no-one can say that," he said.
"We've had a super run (in the Cup Winners' Cup), but now we must turn the European page."
